-    Pityriasis rosea: 2–3x/day for up to 3 wk for pruritus (PO antihist PRN) - systemic glucocorticoids ⍉routine tx (relapse risk)
-    Psoriasis: lrg patches <10% BSA → high-potency to ultra-high-potency topical steroid creams or ointments - flare-ups remain common → USU combined w additional therapies
-    Contact derm: topical corticosteroids for localized involvement (widespread → systemic corticosteroids)
-    Nonbacterial folliculitis: topical corticosteroids + PO antihist for Sxtomatic tx

-    Simple stomatitis: topical steroids (eg dexamethasone elixir) = 1st-line - most effective started @ Sx onset - erythema multiforme: low-potency topical corticosteroids for skin discomfort (painful oral lesions → high-potency corticosteroid gels)
-    Also: mild pityriasis alba - alopecia areata (eg fluocinolone acetonide cream BID) - vitiligo repigmentation — w calcineurin inhibitors · vitD analogs · emollients · phototherapy as listed
-    SE: topical fluorinated corticosteroids can cause acne
-    Psoriasis: 1st-line - combine w topical calcineurin inhibitors & topical vit D analogs
-    Psoriasis (mild-mod): main tx - betamethasone dipropionate · triamcinolone acetonide
-    Psoriasis - sensitive areas where potent corticosteroids are contraindicated (eg face · genitals) → tacrolimus ointment or pimecrolimus cream
-    Psoriasis: 1st-line w topical corticosteroids & topical vit D analogs
-    Psoriasis: pimecrolimus = 1st-line for face or intertriginous areas
-    Pityriasis alba: w mild topical corticosteroids + emollients
-    Vitiligo: repigmentation w topical corticosteroids · calcineurin inhibitors · vitD analogs · phototherapy
-    Lichen planus: 1st-line topical or PO corticosteroids (by severity) - tx-resistant vulvar dz → topical calcineurin inhibitors

-    Topical (comedonal + mild papulopustular/mixed acne): tretinoin (start 0.025% cream twice wkly @ night → ↑freq to once nightly if tolerable) · adapalene · tazarotene (FDA-approved for plaque psoriasis, acne vulgaris, + photoaging (adjunctive palliation))

-    Isotretinoin (severe acne ⍉responding to topical/PO tx - USU reserved for severe or refractory acne): 20-wk course - ~20% of pts relapse w.in 3 yrs + require a 2nd round - daily dosing over intermittent (lidose or strd)
-    MOA (isotretinoin): shrinks sebaceous glands - ↓sebum secretion - inhibits the sebum-dep bacterium Cutibacterium acnes
-    ⍉ in preg (teratogenic → spont abortions + congenital malformations) - must enroll in iPledge · receive regular preg tests + use 2 forms of contraception

-    SE: dry skin & lips (MC) · dry eyes - ↑TG & cholest - arthralgias · myalgias · hepatitis · leukopenia · premature long bone closure - photosensitivity · ↑DM · HA · idiopathic IC HTN · fatigue · possibly psychiatric
-    Psoriasis: PO retinoids = option for extensive dz
-    Monitoring (isotretinoin): LFTs + lipids only (⍉ ↑neuropsych or IBD risk found)

roles.drugs: Systemic therapy can generally be considered when BSA > 5%, or for psoriatic arthritis: MTX (switch if < 25% PASI improvement @ 4 wks) - cyclosporine for severe dz (mo) - acitretin for severe · pustular or palmoplantar dz (⍉ preg for ≥ 3 yr after)
roles.note: cyclosporine label: psoriasis ⍉established < 18 y - acitretin label: ⍉established in pediatric pts
